html:
SMTO-EXE-0101 — The screen capture was stopped before it finished

GUID: cb916ab9-532f-5151-887d-1496b94960a9
Slug: screen-cancelled
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • SMTO stopped looking at the computer's screen before it finished, usually because the task was stopped. No screenshot or screen text from this attempt was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you selected Stop on the task, this is expected and you don't need to do anything. Stopping a task also stops any screen capture it was in the middle of.
  2. Wait until the task shows it has fully stopped before you ask for anything new. SMTO first finishes cleaning up the stopped capture, so a new request won't overlap with it.
  3. If you still need the screen, send a new message asking SMTO to take a screenshot or read the text on the screen. SMTO never repeats a stopped capture on its own; it only looks at the screen again when asked.

What success looks like

  • The new request finishes and the task shows the screenshot or the screen text.

If it still fails

  • If captures keep stopping when nobody stopped the task, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO and that Gateway. Don't paste screenshots or screen contents into your report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway screen operation saw its cancellation signal before completing the observation, so it stopped and published no screenshot or OCR result.

What this means

  • A screen checkpoint observed cancellation before completing its bounded observation; the worker's existing cleanup path owns termination and any published-artifact cleanup. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • A screen checkpoint observed cancellation before completing its bounded observation; the worker's existing cleanup path owns termination and any published-artifact cleanup.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original request's cancellation and artifact state; partial observation is not a finished capture.

How to fix it

  • Confirm in the Server and Gateway logs that the cancellation came from /screen/cancel (task Stop or run cancellation); the screen worker subprocess is terminated and no artifact is published. If the observation is still needed, issue a new explicit screen.* tool call with a fresh execution ID.
  • No completed observation is established. Start a new explicit request only if the observation is still needed.

Retry and execution caution

  • No completed observation is established. Start a new explicit request only if the observation is still needed.

How to verify the fix

  • The original worker and artifact lifecycle settle before any new explicit observation.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
